title: Requirement
description:
Guiding question: What must Please demonstrably satisfy?

A requirement defines a binding, unambiguous, and verifiable condition concerning the behavior or properties of Please. Requirements describe the agreed product specification independently of implementation progress and validation results. A requirement is binding unless explicitly marked as obsolete. Requirements never name components, tests or code; components and tests name the requirements they implement or verify.

id.description: Permanent, unique identifier. IDs must never be reused.

name.description: Short, descriptive name of the requirement.

area.description:
The part of the product the requirement belongs to, exactly one.

setup: initialization, synchronization and Git hook management.
configuration: configuration files, validation, parameters and limits.
rules: rule definitions, rule sets, execution points, external rule sets, selection and plans.
checks: deterministic checks, concurrency, dependencies, fail-fast and scheduling.
reviews: AI reviews, adapters, review input and review results.
integrity: snapshots, stability, freshness and run context.
reporting: reports, status, progress, terminal output and exit codes.
distribution: release artifacts, versions and installation.

description.description: Defines a binding, unambiguous, and verifiable condition that Please must satisfy, as one statement. It describes required behavior or properties without prescribing unnecessary implementation details.
examples: Please must support importing external rule sets using immutable Git commit references.

rationale.description: One sentence in plain language on why the product needs this requirement, written for an owner who reads it without the code. A requirement whose reason does not fit into one sentence is probably not significant enough and should be merged with another or dropped.
examples: Without it, a user could read a progress line as proof that a rule was checked when it never ran.

decisions.description: Decisions that shaped this requirement. Omit the property when no significant choice stands behind the requirement.

obsolete.description: Marks a requirement as historical and no longer binding. Omit this property for active requirements.
